content:
I've been wanting some common category of automata/machines, would mathlib be a good place for that to exist? Specifically a category with morphisms as stream functions or mealy machines, which I think would be generally useful in formalizing things like circuits or programming languages.

Some standard nomenclature I've come across is the Mac category from Bicategories of Automata, Automata in Bicategories and more primitive categories of mealy machines/stream functions in older papers, which I think might be nice to have as Machine or Automata in CategoryTheory

I think I can factor out a lot of the code from this category of sequential circuits into a more general category so most of the work should hopefully just be refactoring.

This would most likely require a TracedCategory class and Causal prop:
#36853
#37644

Trying to put into Mathlib would probably be a very frustrating experience because you will have a very hard time finding reviewers for this. I recommend trying CSLib if there are indeed well-known applications to computer science, or build your own library otherwise.

Categorical semantics is how I originally ended up working on CSlib, so I can review applications like this, though the general category theory definitions it uses should first be in Mathlib I think. Otherwise there's bound to be duplicate work or very specific definitions that are "categorical" but so closely mirror syntax as to not be generally useful.

Thanks for the pointers! That direction sounds great to me :smiley: I just noticed Cslib already has support for the computability of automata so maybe this could end up fitting in.

I put up a PR for Cslib based on Minimal realization of machines in closed categories. This implementation wound up being simpler and more general than I thought, it adds a Machine as a closed symmetric monoidal category (so no traced/causal functions needed).
